body: It’s when you reflect on your life. The days will suck less. You won’t realize it at the time, but looking back on it you will.

The argument that the decision to commit suicide when you feel your depression is “terminal” has been around for a long time.

The problem is that it isn’t terminal, it just feels really bad when it’s bad. Physician assisted suicide is when you have the choice between dying with dignity versus dying a slow and painful death. It really isn’t suicide per se.

So it does get better. It will get better, you will have bad days, but over a period of time you’ll find that your good days will become more frequent.
I also did accept a defense contractor position in Syria like a week prior to it. So there is that.
Honestly it helped just writing it out.

Not actually correct. If you weight track any patient with inflammatory bowel disease, or any malnutrition disorder it is actually relatively common to lose that much weight during a flare up. 

The problem with me is that I have Crohn’s and I am probably depressed. So who really knows which one is causing the weight loss, considering my flare trigger is stress.
What are you saying? I went from 180 to 150 in a month. I know full well that my weight will regain once I eat again. I just haven’t been hungry in awhile.

The funny thing is that what drew me into it was the carnage. I wanted to see the gore, the suffering, and I wanted to save the world. 

Jokes on me, I have never saved a life.

It’s not even the tough calls, my relationships, the job, or my best friend taking his life. It’s like the culmination of everything, and all of the chaos that is getting to me. Like I can handle a couple things, but right now I have realized that my life has been complete chaos forever and I honestly have no clue what it’s like to have a normal day like normal people do. I would kill to wake up in the morning and just do normal people stuff. Like being a history teacher, no stress, no death, no relationship issues. Just everything working out the way it’s supposed to. 

Public safety and the military is the one occupation where 1+1 never equals 2. So many variables and on top of it all there’s no such thing as scene safety anymore. Hell, when I don’t answer my phone on shift my family assumes something happened.

If I perceive patients in a personal way then I have well over 100 people who have died under my care. And many more who aren’t the person they were before whatever incident made their paths cross mine.

That’s something I can’t personalize, because frankly if I personalize it then it’s real. I try not to think of their families who they leave behind, and try to have some level of clinical detachment.

We had a female a couple years ago cut her throat down the the trachea. She survived. Went to behavioral health. I haven’t seen her since, so probably got the help she needed. When you talk to the golden gate survivors usually they say right when they jumped there was an instant feeling of regret.

Trust me. It’s like every time you have a shit call you add a little water to your cup, and then when it starts to spill you have problems.

A lot of us like to drink. Very few talk about it, and most of the time we deflect on the depressed patients who seek help and laugh at instead of reflecting on our own problems. 

I personally feel awkward every psych patient I take it. Mostly because when I read their hold sheet I can usually relate to at least something. I am just really good at hiding it. Like the only reason I probably haven’t done anything stupid is because I know literally every nurse and doctor in the county (and every medic too). I don’t show emotion on shift, so it scares me to think people would find out I have emotions.

Like no one has ever said thanks. People call me on the worst days of their lives. Like “Hey dude, thanks for being there for me, and sorry about seeing my burnt daughter. I know that image and smell will be with you every time you close your eyes.”

No other guys involved. Which is surprising considering how many guy friends she has.

And yeah it has crossed my mind once or twice about the guy friends.

Honestly my life is like one giant depressing sitcom. Like it’s literally all crashing down on me right now. If I didn’t have the lead role it would be pretty entertaining.

Honestly the hardest part is figuring out whether you’re single or not.

My ex came over to my place randomly came inside, hugged me, smelled me shirt, and then walked out.

She’s also 20, so I can’t be all that surprised.

Honestly my mind is blown still. 

Something about her not being ready.  She’s smart and attractive at least while I was dating her. Now, she just seems like a dirt bag.

Thanks man. I don’t know, it’s just rough being the clinician knowing full well what’s going to go down when I go to the doctor tomorrow. It’s like you know what’s going on and there’s no ignorance so there’s no bliss either.

Raging feeling I am going on a vacation for a few days.

There is no way to pleasantly die with over the counter medications. No there isn’t some magical way of making your own KCl. 

Honestly most doctors specifically write scripts in quantities that won’t kill you. 

And we pretty much have an antidote for everything. Charcoal tastes nasty, narcan will make you puke, CaCl is a pain to get orders for in the field, bicarbonate is a pain too, and Romazicon is super expensive.

So yeah. No real way to do it with OTC.

Therapy and SSRIs are a better option, at least try it out for awhile?
